info.title: Task Service API
info.description: CRUD API for tasks built with clean architecture. Supports task chains with recurrence schedules (every N-th day, every even/odd day, every N-th month day, sparse dates).

tags.name: Task Chains
tags.description: Operations for generating and managing chains of tasks from a master task

post.description:
Creates a new task. If `deadline` is sent, `start_at` is also required. `deadline` must be after `start_at`.

If `chain_generation` is provided, the created task becomes a **master task** with the given schedule, and a chain of recurring tasks is generated according to the schedule. The response contains the master task (the generated chain is stored but not returned directly).

**Field usage notes:**
- For `sparse_dates` schedule: the `start` and `end` fields in `chain_generation` are **ignored** (generation window is not applied). Workday filtering is **not** performed.
- For other schedule types (`every_nth_day`, `every_nth_monthday`, `every_even_day`): `start` and `end` define the generation window (inclusive-exclusive). Only workdays within the window are considered.
- If `start` is omitted, it defaults to the current time. If `end` is omitted, it defaults to `start + 3 months`.

put.description:
Updates an existing task. If `deadline` is sent, `start_at` is also required. `deadline` must be after `start_at`.

**Important:** Changing `start_at` or `deadline` will break the link to the master task (the task becomes standalone).

Setting `make_standalone` to `true` explicitly removes the link to the master task.

If the task is a master task (has a schedule), updating its `title` or `description` will automatically propagate these changes to all dependent tasks with `status = new` in its chain.

**Note:** The `chain_generation` field is ignored in update requests. To modify a task's schedule, use the chain endpoints (`POST /tasks/{id}/chain` to replace the chain or `PUT /tasks/{id}/chain` to propagate).

This endpoint cannot change the task's schedule.

get.summary: Get task chain by master ID
get.description: Returns all tasks that belong to the same chain as the given task (including the master task itself).

post.description:
Turns an existing task into a master task and generates a chain of recurring tasks based on the provided schedule. The original task is updated to become the master (its `master_task_id` is set to NULL and the schedule is attached).

If the task is already part of a chain (i.e., it has dependent tasks), the request fails unless the chain consists only of the task itself.

**Field usage notes:**
- For `sparse_dates` schedule: the `start` and `end` fields in the request body are **ignored** (generation window is not applied). Workday filtering is **not** performed.
- For other schedule types (`every_nth_day`, `every_nth_monthday`, `every_even_day`): `start` and `end` define the generation window. Only workdays within the window are considered.
- If `start` is omitted, it defaults to the current time. If `end` is omitted, it defaults to `start + 3 months`.

201.description: Generated task chain (including the master task)

put.description:
Extends an existing task chain by generating new tasks after the latest existing task (or from an optional custom start date) using the master task's schedule. The schedule must already be defined on the master task.

If `start` is not provided, the generation starts from the latest `start_at` among existing chain tasks (excluding the master).

**Field usage notes:**
- For `sparse_dates` schedule: the `start` and `end` fields are **ignored**. The endpoint will generate all tasks from the `sparse_dates` list that have not yet been created (no filtering by date window).
- For other schedule types: `start` and `end` define the generation window (only workdays within the window are considered). If `end` is omitted, it defaults to `start + 3 months`.

201.description: Extended task chain (all tasks, including existing and newly generated)

description.example: Collect release notes and check migrations

master_task_id.description: ID of the master task if this task belongs to a chain. If `null`, the task is a master task.

schedule.description: Recurrence schedule. Only present on master tasks.

start.description: Start of the generation window (inclusive). Defaults to current time. **Ignored for `sparse_dates` schedule.**

end.description: End of the generation window (exclusive). Defaults to `start + 3 months`. **Ignored for `sparse_dates` schedule.**

ChainPropagation.description: Parameters for extending an existing task chain.

start.description: Optional custom start date for generation. If not provided, generation starts from the latest `start_at` among existing chain tasks. **Ignored for `sparse_dates` schedule.**

end.description: End of the generation window (exclusive). Defaults to `start + 3 months` if not provided. **Ignored for `sparse_dates` schedule.**

Schedule.description: Recurrence schedule for generating a task chain. Exactly one of the fields must be provided.

sparse_dates.description: Generate tasks only on the specified dates (no workday filtering, no generation window).

every_nth_day.description: Generate a task every N-th day (workdays only, respects generation window).

every_nth_monthday.description: Generate a task on the N-th day of each month (workdays only, respects generation window).

every_even_day.description: If true, generate tasks on even-numbered days; if false, on odd-numbered days (workdays only, respects generation window).
